title: Where the Rivers Meet
teaser: Turquoise water, a pink house on the hill, the Chief's long-lost brother, and the vote for the crown.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tobago. Water the colour of a peacock's throat, sand like sugar, and a pink house on the hill above Castara Bay.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: So. The children my brother collected. Come, come. There's fish on the fire and rum in the shade.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I'm Marcus, Gideon's little brother. Our mother was from Trinidad. He got the empire and I got the sea. I think I got the better deal.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I'm sorry about the boy from the creeks. Gideon wrote about him every Christmas.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Gideon said the Lawan girl could count the stars and tell you which ones were missing. I'm so sorry.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: The Lagos boy. Gideon said he was all ambition and no peace. I hope he has peace now.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I have the last seal, and his last instruction: you choose. Together.

choices.text: Raise a glass to Chief Gideon.

response.speaker: marcus
response.text: To my big, loud, impossible brother.

choices.text: Raise a glass to everyone this crown has cost.

response.speaker: marcus
response.text: To Oliver. To all of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then a seaplane lands in the bay, and out steps Ibiere Okoro in purple lace and a temper.

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: You called me a murderer in my own house. I'm here to make sure none of you wear his crown.

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: I'm not here to fight. I didn't know about the money. I didn't know about any of it.

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: I didn't know him at all, it seems. But I want his wish carried out.

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: And I know what the Lagos boy did. Elise's lawyers sent me everything.

choices.text: Apologise. You were wrong about her.
Stand your ground. Let her fight it in court.

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: Then I'll see you in court. All of you.

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: Thank you. He would have liked that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sunset. The sky turns pink, then gold, then violet. Steel pan drifts up from the village.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: One crown. The ships, the tin, the cloth, the banks. Everything my brother built goes to whoever you choose.

scenes.prompt: Who wears the Crown of the Confluence?

response.speaker: marcus
response.text: Then wear it well. It's heavier than it looks.

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: Me? A girl who sells stones in Jos?

choices.text: "Nobody. A council of the houses, every voice equal."

response.speaker: marcus
response.text: Ha! He'd have hated that. Which is how I know it's right.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three months later. The same beach, the same pink sky, a hundred lanterns in the palms.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: {pov} and Nabyen Dalyop are married barefoot in the sand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nabyen Dalyop marries Tari Ebiowei barefoot in the sand. He finally brings her a fish. It's enormous.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nabyen Dalyop marries Kolade Balogun barefoot in the sand. Lagos sends three hundred guests and a live band.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Look at us. A girl from the rocks, married on a beach on the other side of the world. I'm the happiest woman between Jos and Tobago.

lines.speaker: kaneng
lines.text: My daughter. Look at you. Your father would have cried. Loudly.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The bride wears a crown of coral and gold. Confluence Holdings has never had a chairwoman before. It does now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The bride wears a crown of coral and gold. Confluence Holdings has never had a chairwoman before. It does now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the head table sit the four houses, every voice equal, and nobody wearing a crown at all.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Some stories end in blood. This one ends in dancing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Port Harcourt. The top floor of Confluence Tower, looking over the Bonny River.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: {pov} sits at the head of the table. No crown, just the whole empire in one pair of hands.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ships, tin, cloth, money. Four rivers, one hand.

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: He'd be proud. Terrified, but proud.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some nights the tower is very quiet. Power is a beautiful view from a lonely room.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every year after that, on the day the Chief died, the houses meet at the pink house in Tobago.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Jos brings gemstones. The creeks bring fish. Kano brings cloth, and Lagos brings far too much champagne.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They always set one extra place at the table.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: My brother built an empire. You built a family. That's much harder.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They scatter the ashes on the water at dawn, the way he would have wanted.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: He promised me a fish. A big one. He never got to keep his promise.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Lagos never sleeps. Neither do I, anymore.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crown is decided. It weighs more than anything Nabyen has ever carried.

lines.speaker: kaneng
lines.text: Come home to the rocks, my daughter. Rocks don't leave.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Elise kept her word, even from a cell. Her lawyers made sure the board voted the way she'd promised.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kolade Balogun wears the Crown of the Confluence in a glass tower on Victoria Island.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody from Jos, the creeks or Kano ever takes his calls again.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: I earned it, old man. Just like you said.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The view is spectacular. The rooms are very, very empty.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Six months later. The top floor of Confluence Tower, the whole city lit up below like money.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: {pov} and Nabyen Dalyop run the empire together. Boardrooms go quiet when they walk in.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nabyen Dalyop and Tari Ebiowei run the empire together, from the Plateau to the creeks. Boardrooms go quiet when they walk in.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nabyen Dalyop and Kolade Balogun run the empire together. Lagos has never seen a partnership like it, and Lagos has seen everything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Rivals sign whatever is put in front of them. Ministers return their calls within the hour.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: They're afraid of us, you know.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: They're afraid of you. I'm just the one who gets to hold your hand.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: Let them be afraid. I only care that you come home at night.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Love, it turns out, is the most dangerous alliance of all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They never stopped arguing. Not in London, not on the mountain, not on the beach in Tobago, where it finally ended in a kiss that silenced the steel band.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: You still drive me mad, you know.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Good. Keep up, Mr Balogun.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: Twenty years of fighting with you. I want fifty more.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Don't think this means you win the argument.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every argument since has ended the same way.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nabyen Dalyop takes her father's chair at the head of the Confluence table. The girl from the rocks of Jos runs ships, tin, cloth and money now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hadiza Lawan takes the Chief's chair at the head of the Confluence table. Kano always knew she'd count everyone's money one day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She answers to no husband, no council and no ghost. The empire has never been better run.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some nights she stands at the window alone, and finds she does not mind at all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Secret ending. One year later: Jos, the rocks at sunrise.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mama Kaneng opens the last letter the Chief ever wrote. It was hidden in the ledger, among the secrets only the curious would find.

lines.speaker: letter
lines.text: Kaneng. I was a coward for thirty years. I built four rivers because I was too afraid to come back to one. Tell our daughter she was the only treasure I never deserved. — Gideon.

lines.speaker: kaneng
lines.text: Foolish, loud, wonderful man.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Come on, Mama. Let's go home.

outcomes.title: The Price of Gold
outcomes.text: Kolade won the crown and lost everyone. Lagos never sleeps, and now neither does he.

outcomes.title: Ashes on the Water
outcomes.text: Love was found and lost on the same mountain. The crown was won. It was not worth it.

outcomes.title: Dangerous Power Couple
outcomes.text: Love and the crown, in the same two pairs of hands. Nobody in four countries dares say no to you.

outcomes.title: Rivalry Turned Passion
outcomes.text: You fought each other across three continents. In the end, the fighting was the love story.

outcomes.title: Where the Rivers Meet
outcomes.text: A wedding on a Caribbean beach. Four houses, one family. Some stories end in blood. This one ended in dancing.

outcomes.title: Solitary Empress
outcomes.text: She took the crown and kept her heart to herself. The empire has never been better run, and she has never been freer.

outcomes.title: The Crown of the Confluence
outcomes.text: You took the crown. The empire is yours, and so is the silence at the top of the tower.

outcomes.title: Four Rivers, One Sea
outcomes.text: No crown. A council. A family that meets on a beach in Tobago once a year, and argues, and laughs, and remembers.

reflections.text: Secret ending unlocked: The Seventh Seal. You found the hidden words, and the letter the Chief was too afraid to send.
Elise Moreau is in a Swiss prison.
Somewhere warm, the wolf is still running. Not for long.
The widow became a friend. Nobody saw that coming.
Ibiere's lawyers are already in court.
There's a secret ending. Find at least four hidden words in one story to unlock it.

s_psalm.title: The Chief's psalm
s_psalm.text: PSALM. Every evening at sunset Marcus hums the Chief's favourite, Psalm 23. 'He made me learn it for both of us,' he says.

m_tobago.title: Castara Bay
m_tobago.text: A pink house, fish on the fire, and the Chief's long-lost brother.

m_wedding.title: Barefoot in the Sand
m_wedding.text: A hundred lanterns, a wedding, and a mother dancing.

k_letters_marcus.title: Forty years of Christmas letters
k_letters_marcus.text: Every one ends the same way: 'Next year, little brother, I'll come.' He never did.
